items.stem: Why does wind power available to a turbine rise with the cube of wind speed?

options.text: Kinetic energy flux scales with velocity cubed, so small speed gains yield large power gains
options.rationale: Power in the wind is proportional to air density, area and the cube of wind speed.

options.text: Because turbine blades double in length as wind rises
options.rationale: Blade length is fixed; it does not change with wind speed.

options.text: Because air density triples in strong wind
options.rationale: Air density changes little; the cube law comes from velocity.

options.text: Because the generator adds energy proportional to speed
options.rationale: The generator converts, it does not add, energy.

items.explanation: Power in the wind is proportional to air density, area and the cube of wind speed.

items.stem: Which TWO are correct about a turbine's cut-in and cut-out speeds? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Below cut-in speed the turbine produces no useful power
options.rationale: There is too little energy to overcome losses below cut-in.

options.text: Above cut-out speed the turbine shuts down to protect itself
options.rationale: Cut-out protects the machine from excessive loads in high winds.

options.text: Between cut-in and cut-out the turbine always runs at nameplate power
options.rationale: Output follows the power curve and only reaches rated power above rated speed.

options.text: Cut-out speed is where efficiency first reaches the Betz limit
options.rationale: Cut-out is a protection threshold, unrelated to the Betz limit.

items.explanation: There is too little energy to overcome losses below cut-in.

items.stem: What does the Betz limit tell us about a wind turbine?

options.text: No turbine can extract more than about 59% of the kinetic energy in the wind
options.rationale: The Betz limit caps the theoretical fraction of wind energy any rotor can capture.

options.text: Turbines can capture 100% of the wind's energy with perfect blades
Offshore turbines are exempt from the limit
options.rationale: The Betz limit applies regardless of location.

options.text: It sets the maximum legal tip speed
options.rationale: It is a physical efficiency bound, not a regulation.

items.explanation: The Betz limit caps the theoretical fraction of wind energy any rotor can capture.
